title: Applications of Capillary Electrophoresis in the Simultaneous Determination of Oral Antidiabetic Drugs in Pharmaceutical Formulations and Biological Samples: A Review
content: The increasing use of fixed-dose combinations in the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus presents analytical challenges due to differences in the physicochemical properties and concentration ratios of the active pharmaceutical ingredients. Capillary electrophoresis (CE) offers an alternative to chromatographic methods, with advantages including high separation efficiency and low reagent and analyte consumption. This review examines the application of CE to the simultaneous determination of oral antidiabetic drugs in pharmaceutical formulations and biological samples, focusing on separation conditions, analytical performance, and method limitations. A structured literature search covering publications from January 2001 to November 2026 was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect. Studies describing CE-based methods for the simultaneous analysis of oral antidiabetic drugs, including combinations with other pharmaceutical compounds, were considered. The reviewed methods included capillary zone electrophoresis (CZE), micellar electrokinetic chromatography (MEKC), non-aqueous capillary electrophoresis (NACE), microemulsion electrokinetic chromatography (MEEKC), and CE coupled with mass spectrometry (CE-MS). CZE was mainly applied to pharmaceutical formulations, including combinations with drug dosage ratios of up to 500:1, while MEKC provided additional selectivity for mixtures containing neutral analytes. Fewer studies addressed biological samples, where CE-MS and on-line preconcentration techniques were used to improve detection sensitivity. Overall, CE has demonstrated its applicability to the simultaneous determination of oral antidiabetic drugs, particularly in pharmaceutical formulations. However, applications to clinical samples remain limited, and further studies are needed to establish the suitability of these methods for routine analysis.
